sources.title: Enforcement appeal submission changes coming soon
sources.role: Planning Inspectorate digital submission transition notice
sources.facts: Published 10 April 2026; paper enforcement appeal forms ceased and online submission became required during May-June 2026.
sources.guard: Submission channel and rollout date do not prove appeal validity, acceptance, merits or outcome.

sources.title: New digital service becomes the primary route for planning and enforcement appeals
sources.role: Current appeal-service route and supported-type notice
sources.facts: Published 16 April 2026; most planning and enforcement appeals use the new service while some specialist types remain unsupported.
sources.guard: Service availability does not prove jurisdiction, deadline compliance, completeness or successful submission.

sources.title: Make an appeal to the Planning Inspectorate and associated guidance
sources.facts: Collection lists planning, enforcement, listed-building, lawful-development, CIL, planning-obligation and other appeal routes.
sources.guard: Catalogue presence does not prove a right of appeal for a particular applicant, site or decision.

sources.title: Planning appeals procedural guide for applications dated on or after 1 April 2026
sources.role: Current procedural guide for post-1-April-2026 applications
sources.facts: Guide separates post-1-April-2026 cases and describes section 78 rights and Part 1/Part 2 procedures.
sources.guard: Procedure classification does not establish standing, admissibility, evidence sufficiency or appeal success.

sources.title: Certificate of lawful use or development appeals procedural guide
sources.facts: Last updated 20 May 2026 to reflect online-only submission and responsibilities of parties.
sources.guard: Procedural guidance does not prove that the underlying use or development is lawful.

sources.title: Appeal against a planning decision
sources.role: Public eligibility and timing guide for planning appeals
sources.facts: Explains refusal, objectionable conditions and non-determination routes, including different timescales for major projects.
sources.guard: Generic eligibility information does not resolve exact dates, decision scope, ownership or case-specific standing.

sources.title: Lawful development certificates
sources.role: Planning Practice Guidance on existing and proposed lawfulness
sources.facts: Explains sections 191-193 certificates and limits, including other regulatory requirements and material-change risk.
sources.guard: A certificate applies only to planning lawfulness within its stated facts and does not replace building, heritage, licensing or permitting controls.

sources.title: When is permission required?
sources.role: Planning Practice Guidance on permitted development and Article 4 directions
sources.facts: Explains that Article 4 directions can withdraw specified permitted-development rights across a defined area.
sources.guard: General permitted-development or Article 4 guidance does not prove the exact current direction, boundary, conditions or prior-approval result for a parcel.
